name: yylo-dev/yylo
summary: Git-native control plane for Codex and other coding agents that separates agent execution from integration authority, using dedicated worktrees, task leases, receipts, and guarded ref updates to keep parallel work from overwriting changed state.
evidence: README describes YYLO as a command-line orchestrator for coding agents, repeatable workflows, and receipt-backed repository changes, aimed at developers who want a quick agent loop and operators who need typed task, validation, merge, and release-readiness boundaries.

Model alias table targets Codex models (`openai-codex/gpt-5.6-luna`, `openai-codex/gpt-6-astra`) alongside Anthropic models, and notes that alias mappings are subagent-specific, for example Pi and Codex do not share the same `:mini` mapping.

Typed task lifecycle: `task start` freezes the protected target SHA and creates a dedicated branch/worktree; `task preflight` is a read-only closure-defect check before `task finish` queues the committed tip; `merge land` selects one immutable task source, composes in a private detached candidate, and uses Git expected-old ref protection.

Merge itself launches no models, chooses no reviewers, and schedules no suites; `watch exec` emits machine-readable run receipts with state, exit code, and log bytes; the seven shipped agent skills install into `.agents/skills`, `.claude/skills`, and `.pi/skills`.
